test_completeness.enumeration_basis: One row per acceptance criterion AC-1..AC-6 in .shipwright/planning/iterate/2026-07-24-terminal-gpu-off-by-default.md, plus each distinct behavioural branch introduced by the diff (resolver polarity, factory parameter, settings persistence, scroll-heal gating, back-compat).

behaviors.note: The GPU-side texture eviction/repack that corrupts the atlas does not reproduce off a real GPU (SwiftShader does not evict) - same residual as #206/#215. The WIRING is fully tested above; the visual outcome is the user's confirmation.

behaviors.behavior: AC-6 Visual baselines regenerated for the renderer flip; only intended routes changed
behaviors.evidence: visual-baselines workflow run 30127239855 (pinned Linux container) against the pushed branch: changed-baselines.txt lists ONLY settings.png (the new GPU checkbox) - committed. task-detail-terminal.png came back BYTE-IDENTICAL, i.e. the CI container was already rendering the terminal without WebGL, so the flip shifted no terminal pixels. No unintended visual bleed.

surface_verification.stack: isolated single-process (built client via SHIPWRIGHT_STATIC_DIR, Hono tsx on 127.0.0.1:3849, temp USERPROFILE)
surface_verification.notes: Renderer change is inherently browser-visible; jsdom cannot distinguish the arms (no canvas getContext). Spec 93 is the differential proof: default arm 0 canvases + renderer=dom, opt-in arm 3 canvases + renderer=webgl. AC-3 is additionally driven through the REAL Settings UI (open /settings, toggle the checkbox, mount a terminal, assert the renderer, then toggle back) after external review flagged that seeding localStorage alone never proved a user can reach the control.
